newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. colleagues happy about Albright's nomination.
newsitem.headline: U.N. colleagues happy about Albright's nomination.

text.p: U.N. ambassadors from Britain, Canada and South Korea immediately expressed their delight on Thursday at seeing their colleague Madeleine Albright named U.S. Secretary of State.
And those who had privately criticised her in the past, particularly for jettisoning Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's re-election, were silent and respectful.
President Bill Clinton on Thursday named the Czech-born Albright, his U.N. ambassador for nearly four years, to be secretary of state and the first woman ever to hold the post.

But she did not mention the United Nations in her comments in Washington accpeting her nomination, although Clinton said that despite difficulties the United States remained committed to the world body.

Britain's U.N. ambassador, Sir John Weston, told reporters, "Personally I am delighted for her. I have worked closely with her in the 15 months I have been in the United Nations. I have grown to like her enormously and to respect her professionally very greatly."

"So far as the United Kingdom is concerned it is a very good development. We have always had secretaries of state who have understood and liked and worked with the United Kingdom and I am very happy that that tradition will continue," he said.
Canada's ambassador Robert Fowler told reporters, "Our relations with her have been exceptionally good. She understands Canada, she understands the world, she understands multilateral diplomaacy.
"She has a remarkable grasp of the issues that we deal with at the United Nations," he said.
South Korea's ambassador, Park Soo Gil, said,"She must be the best qualified candidate for secretary of state particularly because she has a belief in multilateralism so we could not be happier.
"She has a vision for the future of the world and she is an ardent believer in the United Nations system," he added. "I will be the happiest one to congratulate her."

Albright at the United Nations has had her successes and been the subject of biting criticism, never more so than when she vetoed a second-term for Boutros-Ghali while her 14 Security Council colleagues voted for him in a November poll.

She also has had to cope with a mounting U.S. debt of more than $1 billion to the world body which undercuts her criticism of Boutros-Ghali for not spending enough time on reforming the United Nations.

While critical of the United Nations, she has also dismissed criticism by radical groups in the United States that the world body was about to turn into a world government. "I don't think the U.N. is going to descend upon us in black helicopters in the middle of the night and steal our lawn furniture" she once said during a speech in North Carolina.
Clinton in his remarks slipped and said Albright was sent to the United Nations because "I thought she would make a good secretary-general."

Responding to laughter, he said to her "You don't want that job." This prompted Vice President Al Gore to quip "though she does speak French," a dig at Paris's insistence than any successor to Boutros-Ghali should speak good French.
